newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ABARE sees 97/98 Australian nickel output up.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ABARE sees 97/98 Australian nickel output up.

text.p: Australia's mine nickel production is expected to rise 11.9 percent in the 1996/97 year to June 30, with exports up 31.2 percent, Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said on Tuesday.
In its March quarterly report, ABARE forecast nickel production at 132,000 tonnes in 1997/98, up from an estimated 118,000 in 1996/97, which would be up 11 percent on 1995/96.
ABARE said the forecast reflected the startup of new projects including Silver Swan, operated by Outokumpu Oy, Cawse, operated by Centaur Mining NL, and Yakabindie, operated by Dominion Mining Ltd.

Australian production of refined nickel is forecast to rise to 72,000 tonnes in 1997/98 from 69,000 in 1996/97, largely as a result of higher output from WMC Ltd and the start of operations by new producers.

The bureau, the Australian government's main commodities forecasting agency, said world production is expected to rise by 3.2 percent to 979,000 tonnes in calendar 1997 and to rise further to 1.01 million tonnes in 1998.
Nickel prices are forecast to increase by seven percent in 1997, to average US$8,025 per tonne or 364 U.S cents per pound, before rising to $9,000 (408 cents/lb) in 1998.
"Nickel prices are traditionally volatile and uncertainties over the strength of demand in some OECD countries and the timing of new supply are likely to sustain that volatility," ABARE said.
ABARE said world consumption of primary nickel is expected to rise by 5.6 percent in 1997 to 993,000 tonnes, reaching 1.02 million tonnes in 1998.
